caption: What if every bee on Earth vanished overnight? There are over 20,000 kinds of bees, and a single worker honey bee makes only about 1/12 of a teaspoon of honey in her whole life. About 75% of crop types get at least some help from pollinators like bees. But the big staples, wheat, rice and maize, don't need bees at all, so roti and chawal would be safe. Researchers estimate that losing ALL pollinators would cut world crop output by roughly 5 to 8%. Not a famine, but melons, kiwis and many nuts would become rare and pricey. In parts of Sichuan, China, people already hand-pollinate apple flowers with brushes. Good news: chocolate survives, because cacao flowers are pollinated by tiny midges, not bees. Plot twist: that viral 'Einstein said humans would last 4 years without bees' quote? There's no proof he said it. It first showed up in 1965, 10 years after he died.
